Leia uma linha de palavras separadas por: Read a line of words separated by spaces and print how many DIFFERENT words it has. Use a `Set`.
Um Set guarda cada valor uma única vez:: A Set stores each value only once: when we build it from the list, the repeated ones vanish and `size` gives the number of different values.
Leia uma linha de palavras separadas por: Read a line of words separated by spaces. Print the word that appears most and how many times it appears, separated by a space. In case of a tie, print the alphabetically smallest (plain string comparison). Use a `Map` to count.
O Map associa palavra → contagem: para c: The Map associates word → count: for each word, add 1 to the existing value (or to 0). Then we go through the pairs keeping the best, and on a tie the alphabetically smaller word wins.
Leia duas linhas de palavras separadas p: Read two lines of words separated by spaces. Print three lines: `Comum: ` with the words that are in BOTH lines, `Só na primeira: ` with those only in the first line and `Distintas: ` with the total number of different words. The lists come out in alphabetical order separated by spaces; an empty list appears as `-`.
Interseção: filtrar os elementos de a qu: Intersection: filter the elements of a that b.has(). Difference: those b does NOT have. Union: spread both into a new Set and read the size. `has` is fast because the Set does not scan the list.
Leia `n` e uma linha com `n` inteiros (p: Read `n` and a line with `n` integers (they may repeat). Print the length of the LONGEST run of consecutive numbers that can be formed from them, in any order (for example, 100 4 200 1 3 2 has 1, 2, 3, 4 → length 4).
Truque: guarde tudo num Set. Só começamo: Trick: put everything in a Set. We only start counting from a number x whose predecessor x − 1 is NOT in the Set (the start of a run); then we count x+1, x+2... while they exist. Each number is visited only a few times: O(n), without sorting.
O Set ignora valores repetidos, mantém a: The Set ignores repeated values, keeps the order in which each value entered for the FIRST time, and add of a value that already exists changes nothing. delete removes the value where it was; a value added later goes at the end.
O Map também lembra a ordem de inserção: The Map also remembers the insertion order of the keys: the order in which each word first appeared. Counting changes the value but not the key's position. After delete, get returns undefined.
Num objeto comum as chaves viram TEXTO:: In a plain object the keys become TEXT: o[1] and o["1"] are the same key (the second assignment overwrites). In Map and Set the types are respected: 1 and "1" are different (and 20 and 20.0 are the same number). In a Set, NaN counts as equal to NaN and 0 as equal to −0. A Set made from a string keeps the letters without repeating.

Escreva o GERADOR `sequencia(n)` (uma `f: Write the GENERATOR `sequencia(n)` (a `function*` that uses `yield`) that produces {0}, in that order. Then read `n` (n ≥ 1) and print, on one line separated by spaces, all the values produced by `sequencia(n)`.
Um gerador é uma função que pode PAUSAR: A generator is a function that can PAUSE at each `yield`, handing over a value. Spreading the generator with [...gen] consumes all the values until it finishes.

Escreva o gerador `valores(limite)` que: Write the generator `valores(limite)` that produces {0}. Read `limite` (≥ 1) and print the produced values on one line, separated by spaces, going through the generator with `for...of`.
O gerador mantém suas variáveis (como a: The generator keeps its variables (like a and b in Fibonacci) between one `yield` and the next. The `for...of` asks for one value at a time until the generator finishes.

Escreva dois geradores: `infinito(k)`, q: Write two generators: `infinito(k)`, which produces WITHOUT END {0}; and `pegar(gen, n)`, which produces only the first `n` values of any generator `gen` and then finishes. Read `k` and `n` (one per line) and print the first `n` values of `infinito(k)`, separated by spaces.
O gerador infinito não gasta memória nem: The infinite generator uses no memory and does not hang because it only computes the next value when someone asks. `pegar` is the one that decides to stop: it counts the values and does `return` on reaching n, and the infinite loop is never consumed beyond that.
Leia duas linhas, cada uma com inteiros: Read two lines, each with integers separated by spaces. Write the generator `intercalar(a, b)`, which produces one element of `a`, one of `b`, another of `a`, another of `b`, and so on; when one list ends, it produces what is left of the other. Print the produced values on one line separated by spaces.
Pegamos um iterador de cada lista (`[Sym: We take an iterator from each list (`[Symbol.iterator]()`) and call `next()` on both in turns. Each result has `done` (finished?) and `value`. When both have finished, the generator ends; while only one has finished, the other continues alone.
Creating the generator (g()) runs nothing. Each next() runs the body up to the NEXT yield, and only then is the value handed to the outer console.log. After the last yield, the following next() runs the rest of the body and returns done: true and value: undefined.
O for...of e o gerador trabalham em reve: The for...of and the generator work in turns: the generator runs up to the yield, the loop uses the value, and only then does the generator continue. On break at v = {0}, the generator is abandoned and the code after the last yield (the last log) NEVER runs.
Leia uma linha com nomes de disciplinas: Read a line with course names separated by spaces, then an integer `m` and `m` lines `<A> <B>`, each saying that `A` is a prerequisite of `B` (there are no repeated lines). For each course, in alphabetical order, print a line `<name>: <how many direct prerequisites it has>`.
O número de pré-requisitos diretos é o G: The number of direct prerequisites is the vertex's IN-DEGREE: we start everyone at 0 and, for each edge A → B, add 1 to B's degree.
Leia uma linha de disciplinas, `m` e `m`: Read a line of courses, `m` and `m` lines `<A> <B>` (A is a prerequisite of B, no repeated lines). Print, on one line separated by spaces and in alphabetical order, the courses that can be taken NOW, that is, those with no prerequisite at all.
As disciplinas disponíveis são as de gra: The available courses are those with in-degree 0. We compute the degrees and filter; the plain sort() already orders the names as text.
Leia uma linha de disciplinas, `m` e `m`: Read a line of courses, `m` and `m` lines `<A> <B>` (A is a prerequisite of B). Choose an order to take ALL of them: at each step, among those available (all prerequisites already taken), take the alphabetically smallest (plain string comparison). Print the order on one line separated by spaces, or `Ciclo` if it is impossible (some prerequisites depend on each other).
É o algoritmo de Kahn: repetimos \"pegar: It is Kahn's algorithm: we repeat "take the smallest course with degree 0, take it and subtract 1 from the degree of whatever depends on it". If at some point there is none with degree 0 but courses remain, they form a cycle.
Leia uma linha de disciplinas, `m` e `m`: Read a line of courses, `m` and `m` lines `<A> <B>` (A is a prerequisite of B). In each semester you can take ALL the available courses at the same time (those whose prerequisites were taken in EARLIER semesters). Print `Semestres: <smallest number of semesters to take everything>` or `Ciclo` if it is impossible.
Truque: Kahn por CAMADAS. Cada camada é: Trick: Kahn by LAYERS. Each layer is the set of courses with degree 0 at that moment; taking them all frees the next layer (those that reach degree 0). The number of layers is the minimum number of semesters. If a course was left at the end, there was a cycle.
Each edge [A, B] adds 1 to B's degree. The lines show: the degree of the requested course, how many have degree 0, and the largest degree.
A cada volta, entre os de grau 0 ainda n: On each turn, among those with degree 0 not yet done, choose the alphabetically SMALLEST, print it and subtract 1 from the degree of what depended on it. Repeat until none is available.
Cada volta do laço é uma camada: todas a: Each turn of the loop is a layer: all the courses with degree 0 at that moment. `total` adds up how many were taken; if it ended up smaller than the number of courses, the ones left depend on each other (cycle).
Uma escada tem `n` degraus e você sobe d: A staircase has `n` steps and you climb 1 or 2 steps at a time. Read `n` and print in how many different ways (the order of the steps counts) you can reach the top. Use a TABLE filled from step 1 to `n`, without recursion.

A staircase has `n` steps and you climb 1, 2 or 3 steps at a time. Read `n` and print in how many different ways (the order of the steps counts) you can reach the top. Use a TABLE filled from step 1 to `n`, without recursion.
tab[i] é o número de maneiras de chegar: tab[i] is the number of ways to reach step i. The last step came from one step below, two below (or three): we add the ways to reach each one. We start from tab[0] = 1 (one way of not climbing).
Leia uma linha com os valores das moedas: Read a line with the coin values (positive, different integers, unlimited quantity of each), then `q` and `q` change amounts (≥ 0), one per line. Compute ONE dynamic programming table up to the largest requested amount and, for each change `v`, print `v: <smallest number of coins>` or `v: impossível`.
min[v] é o menor número de moedas que fo: min[v] is the smallest number of coins that make v. For each value, we try each coin c: if v − c is possible, one option is min[v − c] + 1. We fill the table from the smallest value to the largest, only once, and all the requests come from it.
Leia uma linha com os valores das moedas: Read a line with the coin values (positive, different, unlimited quantity of each), then `q` and `q` values (≥ 0), one per line. For each value `v`, print `v: <in how many different ways v can be formed>`, where ways with the same coins in another ORDER count as one (for v = 0 there is 1 way: using no coin at all).
Truque para não contar a mesma combinaçã: Trick to avoid counting the same combination in different orders: the OUTER loop goes through the coins and the inner one through the values. This way, when considering coin c, we only add ways that use it after the previous coins, in a fixed order.
Problema da mochila. Leia `n` e a capaci: Knapsack problem. Read `n` and the capacity `C` (on the same line) and then `n` lines `<weight> <value>`. Each item can be taken only ONCE. Print the largest total value that fits in a knapsack of capacity `C`.
melhor[c] é o maior valor com capacidade: melhor[c] is the largest value with capacity c. For each item, we update the table backwards (c from cap down to the weight): this way melhor[c − peso] does NOT yet include the current item and it is not counted twice. Going forwards would give the knapsack with unlimited items.
Moedas [{0}]. Preencha de 0 a {1}: min[0: Coins [{0}]. Fill from 0 to {1}: min[0] = 0 and, for each v, the smallest of min[v − c] + 1 among the coins c that fit. A "-" marks impossible values (Infinity).
Moedas [{0}]. Processe uma moeda por vez: Coins [{0}]. Process one coin at a time, from the coin's value up to {1}: formas[v] gains formas[v − c]. After the last coin, formas[v] is the number of combinations that add up to v.
Uma linha por item: a tabela melhor[0..C: One line per item: the table melhor[0..C] after considering that item. Each capacity c becomes the larger of keeping the old value and using the item (weight p, value v) on top of melhor[c − p], which is still the value BEFORE the current item (that is why the loop goes backwards).
Leia `n` (1 ≤ n ≤ 5). Gere, por BACKTRAC: Read `n` (1 ≤ n ≤ 5). Generate, by BACKTRACKING (recursion), all the sequences of `n` symbols `{0}`/`{1}` in which there are NO two `{1}` in a row. Print first the count and then the sequences, one per line, in the order the backtracking finds them (always trying `{0}` before `{1}`).

Read `n` (1 ≤ n ≤ 5). Generate, by BACKTRACKING (recursion), all the sequences of `n` symbols `{0}`/`{1}`. Print first the count and then the sequences, one per line, in the order the backtracking finds them (always trying `{0}` before `{1}`).
A função recebe a sequência montada até: The function receives the sequence built so far. If it already has n digits, it is a solution. Otherwise, it tries adding the first symbol and, if allowed, the second: each attempt is a recursive call, and on return the previous sequence is intact (the text is recreated on each call).
Leia uma palavra de 1 a 4 letras DIFEREN: Read a word of 1 to 4 DIFFERENT letters, already in alphabetical order. Generate, by backtracking, all the PERMUTATIONS of those letters (all possible orders). Print the count and then the permutations, one per line, in alphabetical order (always choosing the smallest available letter first).
Em cada posição tentamos todas as letras: At each position we try all the letters not yet used: we mark the letter as used, call the recursion for the next position and UNDO the mark on return (that is the "back" in backtracking). Since the letters are tried in order, the output already comes out in alphabetical order.
Leia `n` (1 ≤ n ≤ 7). Coloque `n` rainha: Read `n` (1 ≤ n ≤ 7). Place `n` queens on an `n × n` board so that no two attack each other (same column or same diagonal; one per row). Print `Soluções: <how many exist>` and, on the next line, `Colunas: <column of each row, from 1 to n>` of the FIRST solution found (row by row, columns tried left to right), or `Nenhuma solução`.
Colocamos uma rainha por linha. Para cad: We place one queen per row. For each column we test whether the position is safe with respect to the queens already placed (same column or |column difference| = row difference). If it is, we move on to the next row; on returning from the recursion, we try the next column. Reaching row n is a solution.
Leia `H` e `W` e depois `H` linhas com `: Read `H` and `W` and then `H` lines with `W` characters: `.` free and `#` obstacle (the top-left and bottom-right corners are always free). Starting at the top-left corner, moving only RIGHT or DOWN, print in how many different paths you can reach the bottom-right corner without stepping on obstacles.
Em cada célula há duas escolhas (direita: At each cell there are two choices (right or down). Leaving the grid or stepping on an obstacle is worth 0 paths; reaching the destination is worth 1; otherwise, we add the paths of the two choices. For small grids the direct recursion is enough.
Para cada item há duas ramificações: NÃO: For each item there are two branches: NOT taking it (call with the same `atual`) and taking it (adds the item). The first branch is explored entirely before the second, so the empty set comes out first and the last one out is the one that takes all the items.
Cada chamada tenta usar v[i] primeiro e: Each call tries using v[i] first and then skipping. Solutions appear when the sum reaches {0}. The cut `soma > alvo` abandons hopeless paths (pruning). The last line counts ALL the calls, including those that ended in a cut or with no solution.
Para n = {0} existem {1} soluções. `cham: For n = {0} there are {1} solutions. `chamadas` counts each time `colocar` is called, that is, each valid partial position explored ({2} in total, including the initial call and those that reach row n).
